items.title: ESP32 iPhone Agent: a $7 board lets AI operate a real iPhone
items.summary: An open-source project in which a ~$7 ESP32-S3 board streams an iPhone's screen to an AI via AirPlay and operates the phone through USB HID touch input — no computer in the middle, no jailbreak. The current build is portrait ASCII video at 480×1040 and up to about 5fps, and it cannot see a locked screen.

items.title: Murmell AVP: a versioning protocol designed for AI agents
items.summary: A version protocol for several agents writing to the same repository in parallel: each agent's changes are verified and replayed on top of the current main branch, then land as ordinary Git commits, so parallel work collides far less.

items.title: OpenBot: run multiple coding agents side by side in one desktop app
items.summary: A desktop app that runs several coding agents side by side, letting them message each other and hand off files, with a phone app to check in and steer them remotely. Note: its developer preview grants full-disk access by default with no per-action approval, so mind the permissions before trying it.
